findings.where: pigment/crates/ui-egui/src/ai_ui/task_bar.rs:143-144 (expand_from_crop), reached from task_bar.rs:119-121 (crop_item's "Generative Expand" button), drawn by tools/crop_task_bar.rs:67 inside the canvas pass
findings.issue: The Crop task bar's Generative Expand button panics the interface thread on any document wider or taller than 30,000 px. expand_from_crop computes `(w + left + right).round().clamp(w, 30_000.0)` and the same for the height, with `w`/`h` the document's own size. f64::clamp asserts min <= max, so with w > 30,000 the call panics whatever the crop frame is. The panic happens while drawing the canvas, not inside command dispatch or import/export, so no crash guard catches it: the app goes down and unsaved work since the last Data Recovery autosave is lost. PhotoCraft allows canvases up to 300,000 px a side (file.new, Canvas Size, and the engine's ai.generativeExpand all accept that), so a 40,000 px panorama is an ordinary document.
findings.scenario: Connect an OpenAI or Gemini key so that `fits(app, Image)` is true and the button shows. Open or create a 40,000 x 2,000 px RGB document. Choose the Crop tool so a crop frame exists and the contextual task bar is on (the default). Click "Generative Expand" in the Crop task bar. Result: panic `min > max, or either was NaN. min = 40000.0, max = 30000.0` and the process exits with every open document unsaved. The same happens for a document taller than 30,000 px.
findings.test: A ui-egui test (crates/ui-egui/tests/it/ai.rs, which already installs a mock backend with an image key): make a 40000 x 100 transparent document, set app.ui.tool = Tool::Crop and app.ui.crop_rect = Some([0.0, 0.0, 40000.0, 100.0]), then call ai_ui::task_bar::expand_from_crop(&mut app). Before the fix it panics. After the fix it opens the Generate window on ai.generativeExpand with g.width >= 40000 and no panic. A second case with a 20,000 px document and a frame reaching x1 = 45,000 checks the requested width (see the fix).
findings.fix: Do not clamp with the document size as the lower bound against a constant. Use the engine's limit and keep min <= max: `let max = 300_000.0_f64; g.width = (w + left + right).round().max(w).min(max) as u32;` (same for the height), or `clamp(w.min(max), max)`. Then make the Generate window's DragValue ranges (generate.rs:449-451, `w0..=30_000`) use the same 300,000 limit, so a document of 30,000 px or more can still be expanded from the window. Today egui silently swaps the inverted range and caps the request at 30,000, which is smaller than the document, so nothing grows.

findings.where: pigment/crates/automation/src/files.rs:25-31 (open_bytes_with_options) and :41-55 (open_with_options) call photocraft_io directly; callers: crates/automation/src/headless.rs:178-192 (Headless::open_with_approval / open_with_options: `pigment-cli run <file>`, `info`, `batch` at apps/photocraft-cli/src/batch.rs:341-344, the MCP server's open at crates/automation/src/server.rs:787, the headless session MCP falls back to while the app is closed) and apps/photocraft-cli/src/document.rs:44-52 (`pigment-cli convert`). The renderer is installed only by crates/engine/src/legacy_pigment_render.rs:10-13, called only from crates/engine/src/jobs.rs:963 (import_options) and crates/engine/src/cmd/file_cmds/open.rs:86. Fallback in crates/io/src/legacy_pigment/smart.rs:186-210.
findings.issue: On the command line and in MCP's headless sessions, the smart objects of a Pigment 0.1-0.4 document open without their smart filters. The importer draws a smart object through a process-wide renderer that the engine installs (legacy_pigment_render::install). Only the engine's own open paths call install: jobs::import_options and file_cmds::open::import_result_for_open, the paths the desktop app uses. The automation crate's open paths go straight to photocraft_io with ImportOptions::default() and never call it. In a pigment-cli or headless MCP process nothing installs the renderer first, so smart::render takes its fallback: the source is placed by its matrix and every smart filter (blur, sharpen, levels and the rest in filters.rs) is skipped. The import report does not say that the filters were left out. The unfiltered cache is also what gets saved: PhotoCraft does not re-render smart objects when a native file loads, so `run old.pigment --out new.pigment` stores the wrong pixels in the converted file until someone edits that smart object. FORK.md says every open path, the CLI and MCP included, gets the importer with the engine's filters.
findings.scenario: `pigment-cli convert crates/io/tests/fixtures/pigment-0.4/v3-smart-filters.pigment out.png`. Also `pigment-cli run v3-smart-filters.pigment --out out.pigment`, or an agent on `pigment-cli mcp` (switch off, the default) opening the same file and exporting it. Result: the smart object shows its source unblurred and unsharpened, with no levels, and the four smart filters are listed on the layer but not applied. File > Open of the same file in the desktop app shows them applied (legacy_pigment_render's own test measures a mean difference under 3 against the app's picture, and more than twice that without the filters).
findings.test: A test in crates/automation (or apps/photocraft-cli/tests/it) in a fresh process: `files::open(Path::new(".../v3-smart-filters.pigment"))`, flatten it with photocraft_compose::flatten_to_surface to RGBA8, and compare with v3-smart-filters.png as legacy_pigment_render.rs's test does (mean < 3.0). It fails today: the mean matches the unfiltered picture. The CLI variant runs `pigment-cli convert` on the fixture and compares out.png. It has to be its own process, or the first test in its binary, because the renderer is a OnceLock and another test may have installed it already.
findings.fix: Make the install reachable outside the engine, e.g. `pub fn install_legacy_pigment_renderer()` re-exported from photocraft_engine (legacy_pigment_render.rs is Pigment's own file). Call it at the top of photocraft_automation::files::open_bytes_with_options and open_with_options, one `// Pigment:` line each listed in FORK.md, so convert, info, run, batch and MCP all get it. A second call in genai::session (Pigment's file, used by every Headless) costs nothing. Also add a line to the import report when smart::render takes the fallback, so a missing renderer can never again leave out the filters without a word.

findings.where: pigment/crates/engine/src/cmd/ai_cmds/describe.rs:38-43 (the answer is only trimmed); pigment/crates/genai/src/backend.rs:275-278; pigment/crates/ui-egui/src/ai_ui/describe.rs:157-163 (the whole text in a multiline TextEdit) and :90-101 (Use as Document Description writes it to the XMP)
findings.issue: Describe Image puts no limit on the answer. The provider's text is bounded only by the HTTP body cap (DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES, 64 MiB) and reaches the Describe window whole. The Assistant cuts an answer to TEXT_LIMIT (20,000 characters) because "a provider's answer is not trusted to be reasonable"; Describe does not. egui lays out the entire string in the window's TextEdit (one glyph record per character), so a multi-megabyte answer freezes the interface for seconds and takes hundreds of MB to GBs of memory. "Use as Document Description" then writes all of it into File Info's XMP, which every later save carries.
findings.scenario: A provider or proxy answering /v1/responses with a 30 MB output_text (a runaway model, or a misbehaving endpoint behind PIGMENT_AI_BASE_URL_OPENAI). Image > Describe Image… Result: the Describe window opens and the app stops responding while egui lays out 30 million characters, possibly until it runs out of memory. Clicking Use as Document Description adds 30 MB of XMP to the document.
findings.test: An engine test in ai_cmds/tests.rs with the mock backend's describe returning "x".repeat(1_000_000): ai.describe's `text` is at most the cap, cut at a character boundary. A ui-egui test that drives describe::start with the same mock: app.ai.describe.text holds at most the cap.
findings.fix: Cut the description in the engine's describe (so the CLI, MCP and the window all get the same text), e.g. `text.chars().take(DESCRIBE_LIMIT)` with DESCRIBE_LIMIT = 20_000 like the Assistant's TEXT_LIMIT, adding an ellipsis when cut. Optionally also drop control characters other than \n and \t before the text can reach the XMP.

findings.where: pigment/crates/ui-egui/src/ai_ui/task_bar.rs:101-112 (fill_from_bar) with generate.rs:110-136 (open keeps `variations`, `model` and `provider` across features and openings) and generate.rs:186-190 (params sends g.variations)
findings.issue: The selection task bar's Generate sends as many billed requests as the Generate window was last set to, without showing that number. The bar has only a prompt field and Generate; fill_from_bar runs generate::open(FILL, prompt) and generate::start. Neither resets the window's `variations` (Default is 1, but the value survives closing the window), so after one 3-variation fill in the window, every later one-click Generate in the bar sends 3 requests to the provider (3 x the cost) and adds 3 layers. The model typed into the window for another feature also stays in force: `model` is not reset when the feature changes, so a model typed for Generate Image is used by the bar's fill.
findings.scenario: Edit > Generative Fill…, choose Variations 3, Generate, close the window. Later make a selection, type a prompt in the task bar under it and press Generate. Result: three edit requests are billed and three "Generative Fill N" layers appear. Nothing in the bar said it would make three.
findings.test: A ui-egui test with the mock backend that counts edit_image calls: set app.ai.generate.variations = 3, close the window, set app.ai.bar_prompt and call task_bar::fill_from_bar. Today 3 calls are made; after the fix, 1.
findings.fix: Have fill_from_bar send its own params instead of the window's: `app.run(FILL, {"prompt": prompt, "variations": 1})` with the AI Accounts default provider and model, opening the window only to show a blocker. Or show the variations count in the bar. Also reset `model` in generate::open when the feature changes, since image models differ by feature.

findings.where: pigment/crates/automation/src/files.rs:25-29 (open_bytes_with_options: a name ending in photocraft_format::EXTENSION, which is still `pcraft`, goes to photocraft_format::load_from_bytes without the legacy check); used by crates/automation/src/headless.rs:189-192 (workspace-scoped MCP and `pigment-cli serve`)
findings.issue: A Pigment 0.1-0.4 document named *.pcraft fails to open through MCP's and serve's workspace path. FORK.md says a 0.4 document is recognised by its content, whatever it is called, on every open path, and photocraft_io::route checks legacy_pigment::is_legacy first, even for Open As Pigment. Automation's byte path bypasses route for a `.pcraft` name and calls the native loader directly, which refuses a ZIP without manifest.json. The desktop app, the CLI's path-based open (import_file) and the engine all open the same file.
findings.scenario: Rename a 0.4 file to drawing.pcraft and put it in an MCP workspace folder. The agent calls open on drawing.pcraft. Result: a native-format load error (no manifest). File > Open in the app, or `pigment-cli convert drawing.pcraft x.png`, open it.
findings.test: An automation test: files::open_bytes("x.pcraft", <bytes of a fixture such as v3-groups.pigment>) returns Ok with the fixture's layer count. Today it returns Err.
findings.fix: In open_bytes_with_options, take the native shortcut only when `!photocraft_format::brand::is_legacy_pigment(bytes)`, as io's route_forced does. This is a one-line `// Pigment:` hook to list in FORK.md.

checked: Read FORK.md, PKG-ai-final.md, PKG-port-review-L.md and the three other hunters' JSON (no item repeated). Traced, and found sound: the agent gate across every entry point: control.rs handle runs inside ai_ui::as_agent; gate() in run_command_at_depth; AppBackend.admit with agent_now for commands nested in scripts; automation_input set for synthetic clicks and keys, held for the whole UI pass and reset at frame.rs:407 after ai_ui::show; AI Accounts drops every act except Switch and Close under synthetic input; Assistant send refuses agents without allowAgents; ui.menu.invoke of an ai.* id with only a prompt opens the window and sends nothing. Actions, Batch and menu-item steps: UI playback goes through actions_cmds::begin_playback_from (actions.playing > 0), so admitted() refuses ai.* there. The Assistant's blocked list covers file, path, script and profile params, preset deletes and renames, importers, exporters and other documents; Ranges::of skips inverted ranges, so sanitize_value's clamp cannot panic. Jobs: apply_job (snapshot Arc check, closed document, the user's layer selection and active document put back; Generate Image to a new document stays active); cancel_jobs_on at close; no join at exit; one-step history for fill, expand (the sampler map is taken at the start of edit) and generate; Use as Document Description goes through file.fileInfo (one undoable step, XML-escaped, merged). Modes and depths: layered_doc refuses Indexed, Bitmap and Duotone before anything is sent; compose::render gives straight RGBA for CMYK and Lab; layer_surface converts through convert_pixel; the visible_alpha mask honours a disabled mask (values_into returns ones). Importer cross-paths: Place, Open As Smart Object, Edit Contents and smart-source decoding (decode_source to file_cmds::import) install the renderer and route by content; Edit Contents opens in memory without a path, so the legacy save prompt never appears for it; Data Recovery stores and restores through the native format with the original path; control app.save uses save_automation_with (no prompt); the Home screen thumbnail loader only fails to find a preview in a 0.4 file. Web build: the AI windows, task bars, preferences button and menu items are stubs on wasm32; still_legacy is cfg'd; the importer, ai_cmds and legacy_pigment_render use no std::fs, threads or Instant; craft-zip was already compiled for wasm through photocraft-format. Ran only `target/debug/pigment-cli commands --json`, to list command ids and params. The debug binaries predate the importer (02:59 and 03:41 UTC, before d6247d8), so nothing here was reproduced by running; every finding is traced in source. No cargo was run.
